About Care2U Community Services:
Care2U Community Services is a trusted NDIS provider dedicated to supporting individuals with disabilities in living fulfilling and independent lives. We uphold a high standard of care and promote a positive, empowering culture.
 
Role Overview:
We are looking for compassionate, empathetic, and dedicated Residential Care Officer to join our team. In this role, you will provide personal care, assist with daily activities, and support participants' social and community involvement, all tailored to their individual needs. This position offers an immediate start.
 
Key Responsibilities:
- Deliver personal care and support, following a person-centred approach.
- Assist clients with daily living activities, including meal preparation, personal care (e.g., showering, grooming, toileting), and household tasks.
- Provide assistance with community participation, transport, and engagement in social activities.
- Administer medication according to the participant's care plan.
- Maintain clear communication with clients, families, and team members, ensuring dignity and independence are respected.
- Support clients with complex healthcare and behavioral needs.
- Participate in 24/7 rotating shifts, including sleepover shifts.
 
Benefits of Working with Care2U:
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- Ongoing training and career development opportunities.
- Salary sacrifice options.
- Company events and activities.
- Rewards and recognition programs.
- Supportive, empowering, and fun work culture.
- Immediate start available.
 
Qualifications and Experience:
- AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma OR At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications.
- 1-3 years of relevant experience in disability care or aged care services.
- Current NDIS Worker Screening Check, Working with Children Check, First Aid & CPR Certificate.
- A valid Australian driver’s licence and access to a reliable, insured vehicle.
- National Police Check.
- Awareness of the Code of Conduct for employees in Disability services.
- Valid Australian visa with working rights.

Salary: $80,000 - $82,000
 
How to Apply:
Please apply through the Workforce Australia platform, or visit our website at Care2uservices.org to learn more about the company.
 
Join Care2U Community Services and make a difference in the lives of those who need it most.

Position: Meat Inspector
Type: Full-time
Employer: Hilal Meat Products Company Pty Ltd
Location: Echuca VIC 3564
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Hilal Meat Products Company Pty Ltd is a leading Australian meat processing, wholesale and export company specialising in the sourcing, processing, packaging and distribution of premium halal-certified meat products. With operations based in Echuca, VIC, the company supplies a wide range of fresh and frozen beef, lamb, mutton, goat and poultry to domestic wholesalers, retailers, food service providers and international markets. Renowned for its unwavering commitment to quality, food safety and strict halal certification standards, Hilal Meat fosters a collaborative, values-driven workplace culture that prioritises integrity, continuous improvement, employee development and compliance excellence in a fast-paced, modern processing environment.
About the Position:
The Meat Inspector plays a critical role in ensuring the highest standards of product quality, safety and regulatory compliance at Hilal Meat Products Company Pty Ltd. This position involves inspecting animal carcasses, internal organs and processing facilities to identify any quality or health issues, while monitoring hygiene, auditing procedures and verifying adherence to Australian food safety and halal requirements. By safeguarding the integrity of our premium meat products throughout processing, storage and distribution, the Meat Inspector supports the company’s reputation for excellence and contributes directly to consumer trust and successful domestic and export operations.
Key Responsibilities:
Inspecting animal carcasses, internal organs and meat products to identify quality issues, diseases or impurities and ensure compliance with required standards.
Auditing and monitoring quality procedures at processing facilities, cold storage and packing areas to maintain hygiene and food safety standards.
Testing samples of meat products for quality, size, purity and adherence to halal certification requirements.
Ensuring required standards of hygiene are observed throughout storage, processing, packaging and transport.
Providing advice on disease eradication, pest and disease identification, and regulations pertaining to grading, packing and loading of products.
Coordinating with production teams on quality assurance matters and contributing to continuous improvement in processing operations.
Maintaining accurate records of inspections and assisting with regulatory compliance and export documentation as needed.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Required qualifications: An AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma in the field (at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications).
Required experience: A minimum of 1 year of experience within the Meat Inspector occupation or a closely related role.
Required technical and interpersonal skills: Strong knowledge of Australian meat industry standards, food safety regulations and halal certification processes; excellent attention to detail and observational skills for conducting thorough inspections; ability to work effectively in a team environment within a processing facility; strong communication skills for providing advice to producers and colleagues; problem-solving abilities in identifying and addressing quality issues; and a commitment to maintaining high hygiene and compliance standards in a dynamic operational setting.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Job Title: Sales Performance Analyst 
Position: Full-time 
Company: Khanz Auto Hub Pty Ltd
ABN: 69 643 572 632
Location: 345 Greensborough Road, Watsonia, Victoria, 3087
Salary: $79,000 – $81,000 per annum + guaranteed superannuation

About the Company
Khanz Auto Hub is a trusted used car dealership and fleet management service provider with showrooms in Watsonia and Thomastown in Melbourne, Victoria. We specialize in high-quality used vehicles and customized fleet and rental solutions. At Khanz Auto Hub, we work hard to provide our customers with the best used vehicles and exceptional service they can rely on. We ensure our customers leave our dealerships with a vehicle that perfectly suits their lifestyle and budget. 
For fleet management solutions, we cater to both small and large businesses, offering cost-effective rental and management services designed to optimize fleet performance. 
At Khanz Auto Hub, we strive to provide the best used vehicles and reliable after-sales maintenance services, ensuring comprehensive support for our customers. 

Position Description
We are currently seeking a qualified and experienced Sales Performance Analyst to join our team at Khanz Auto Hub. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in analysing sales performance data, inventory turnover, customer insights, and sales team metrics to drive data-informed decisions that optimise profitability, procurement, and overall business performance in our used vehicle dealership and fleet management operations.
The salary for this position ranges from $79,000 to $81,000 per year plus guaranteed superannuation, depending on qualifications, skills, and experience.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:
1.	Analyse sales transaction data across hundreds of annual vehicle sales to identify patterns in vehicle turnover rates, profitability by vehicle type/age/source, pricing effectiveness, seasonal demand variations, customer purchasing behavior, and margin performance to inform procurement and inventory decisions.
2.	Consolidate data from sales transactions, vehicle purchases, refurbishment expenses, and customer records into organized databases enabling analysis of profitability and sales performance patterns.
3.	Analyze inventory turnover by vehicle type, identify slow-moving vehicles, and recommend which vehicle categories to purchase more or less to improve capital efficiency and reduce holding costs.
4.	Analyze refurbishment costs versus sale prices to determine how much to invest in repairs and improvements for different vehicle types to maximize profit margins.
5.	Prepare performance reports and dashboards presenting which vehicles sell best, procurement recommendations, pricing strategies, and sales forecasts to inform business decisions.
6.	Compare different vehicle sources (auctions, wholesale, trade-ins, direct purchases) by analyzing profit margins and sales speed to determine optimal allocation of the annual procurement budget.
7.	Analyze customer data to identify buyer segments (individual, business, fleet), their vehicle preferences and purchasing patterns to guide inventory selection strategies.
8.	Track and analyze sales representative performance metrics including conversion rates, average sale prices, margin achievement, product mix effectiveness, and customer satisfaction to identify best practices, training needs, and performance improvement opportunities.

Essential Requirements:
•	At least a bachelor’s degree or higher qualification.
•	At least 1 year of full-time work experience.
•	Strong analytical and quantitative skills with advanced Excel and experience in dashboards (Power BI, Tableau) and database management.
•	Ability to interpret and communicate complex data to non-technical stakeholders.
•	Experience analysing sales metrics, product performance, customer trends and pricing structures.
•	High attention to detail, accuracy and ability to prioritise multiple tasks.
•	Experience working with ERP/CRM systems and integrating data from multiple sources.
•	Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Job Title: 		Personal Care Assistant
Salary range: 	$79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role:
Our client is a highly respected aged care provider in the Port Broughton region, renowned for its person-centred approach and commitment to enhancing the quality of life for seniors. With a strong reputation for compassionate care and modern, homelike facilities, they provide a supportive environment where residents are treated with dignity, respect, and individuality. We are seeking a full-time Personal Care Assistant to join their dedicated care team. 

This is an opportunity to work in a well-resourced facility that values both its residents and staff, offering long-term career stability and the chance to make a profound difference in the lives of elderly individuals. In this role, you will provide hands-on personal care while fostering meaningful connections with residents, ensuring their physical, emotional, and social wellbeing is prioritised. You’ll be part of a collaborative team that upholds the highest standards of aged care, with ongoing training and professional development to support your growth in the sector.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Resident-Centred Care & Support:
• Deliver high-quality personal care, including assistance with bathing, dressing, mobility, and mealtime support, tailored to each resident’s individual care plan.
• Promote independence and dignity by encouraging residents to participate in daily activities at their comfort level.
• Provide emotional support and companionship, engaging residents in meaningful conversations and recreational activities.
• Assist with specialised care needs, including dementia support, palliative care, and behavioural interventions under the guidance of registered nurses.

Health Monitoring & Documentation:
• Observe and report any changes in residents' physical or emotional condition to senior staff in a timely manner.
• Accurately document care provided and contributed to care plan reviews to ensure resident needs are continuously met.
• Support therapy and wellness programs, including gentle exercises, cognitive stimulation activities, and social outings.

Safety & Compliance:
• Adhere strictly to infection control protocols, workplace health & safety policies, and Aged Care Quality Standards.
• Maintain a clean and hazard-free environment, ensuring resident rooms and communal areas meet hygiene standards.
• Participate in emergency response procedures, including fire drills and first aid interventions when required.

Team Collaboration & Communication:
• Build trusting relationships with residents’ families, providing updates on care and addressing concerns with empathy and professionalism.
• Work closely with nurses, allied health professionals, and other care staff to ensure a holistic approach to resident wellbeing.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by sharing feedback and participating in staff meetings and training sessions.

Skills & Experience Required:
• Certificate III in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent qualification.
• Minimum 1 year of full-time experience in a similar role.
• NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (issued within the last 5 years) is preferable.
• Up-to-date flu vaccination and full COVID-19 immunisation.
• Satisfactory police check with no disclosures.
• Own reliable transportation.
• Strong teamwork skills and a commitment to long-term employment.

Why You'll Love Working here:
• Rewarding work that makes a real difference in residents' lives
• Ongoing training and professional development opportunities
• Supportive team culture with regular staff recognition
• Modern facilities with quality resources
• Career growth potential within our organization

How to Apply:
Submit your resume and cover letter addressing your experience with the EYLF and your approach to play-based learning. Successful applicants will require valid working rights and must pass background checks.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Temporary - Part Time - up to 5 February 2027

About the Role: 

An exciting opportunity is presented to work within the Northern Adelaide Local Health Network as a Support Services Attendant within the Forensic Mental Health Division. 

The Support Services Attendant is responsible for a high standard of work, providing a timely, efficient, and effective general service undertaking duties in a range of activity areas as described in this duty statement.

The Support Services Attendant may be required to work within several areas of the Health Service including kitchen, laundry, and housekeeping. Support Services Attendants at this level will have limited experience in the catering industry, however, may apply specific knowledge gained through prescribed training and experience.

About You: 

In this role you will have strong interpersonal and communication skills which will enable you to successfully problem solve, resolve conflicts and negotiate, including the ability to engage in difficult conversations, whilst building and maintaining relationships. An ability to effectively manage multiple, diverse and competing priorities and demonstrated resilience within a stressful and complex environment is essential to this role. 

You will be joining a dynamic and expanding Local Health Network that is committed to delivering contemporary, innovative and high-quality health services within modern facilities. 

This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a passionate, highly driven, dedicated and progressive team. 

About Adelaide: 

Adelaide is consistently recognised as a city that artfully combines its compact charm and world-class cuisine with picturesque nature escapes. Ranked one of the worlds "Most Liveable Cities" and "Most Beautiful Cities", Adelaide provides something for everyone combining a wonderful mix of nature with nearby beaches, rolling hills and wildlife and culinary delights with fine dining restaurants, award-winning cafes, bustling food markets and booming boutique bars. Events like the LIV Golf, SANTOS Tour Down Under, Adelaide Fringe and the Adelaide Cabaret Festival add extra appeal to living here. 

About Us: 

The Northern Adelaide Local Health Network (NALHN) is a leading provider of public healthcare services in South Australia, and one of the largest employers in northern Adelaide. 

NALHN serves over 400,000 people in northern Adelaide with a comprehensive range of high-quality healthcare services, including emergency, surgical, obstetric, neonatal, paediatric, oncology, geriatric, palliative care and rehabilitation, and mental health care, as well as primary health care services with a focus on community health promotion and chronic disease management. 

With a commitment for ongoing upgrades to our facilities and the introduction of new services, our priority is delivering exceptional health and wellbeing services that enhance the quality of life for our community. 

With over 7,000 employees, NALHN emphasises quality care and a supportive work environment guided by respect, integrity, and accountability. Our core values foster excellence, innovation, and equitable health outcomes. 

At NALHN Everyone Has a Story, Everyone Matters, Everyone Contributes and Everyone Grows. 

Our Local Health Network Sites and Services: 

NALHN provides a range of hospital (inpatient), outpatient, community and home-based services across multiple sites in Adelaide's north and north-eastern suburbs, including Aboriginal health, mental health, and GP services. 

Lyell McEwin Hospital - the major hospital in northern Adelaide for emergency care, complex and multi-day surgery, medicine, obstetric, paediatrics and outpatient services. 

Modbury Hospital - a general hospital with emergency care, elective surgery, medicine, outpatient and sub-acute services, rehabilitation, geriatric and palliative care. 

Mental Health Services - adult and older persons mental health services and statewide forensic mental health services, across hospital and community settings. 

Watto Purrunna Aboriginal Primary Health Care Services - provides culturally responsive primary healthcare services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in-hospital and across four community sites. 

Primary Health Care Services - including GP Plus sites at Elizabeth, Modbury and Gilles Plains. 
 
Benefits of working at NALHN: 
 
From salary packaging to flexible working arrangements, a large range of opportunities for movement and career progression, you'll find there are lots of benefits of working with Northern Adelaide Local Health Network. 
 
Salary packaging is an option for saving money by paying for some of your everyday expenses from your salary before it is taxed. 
 
Relocation assistance may be available for successful applicants from interstate or overseas. 
 
NALHN supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions. 
 
SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence. 
 
We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if you have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best. 
 
The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working including part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role. 
 
Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check. 
 
Check: 

National Police Check (National Police Certificate) for vulnerable person-related employment screening - apply to any of the accredited bodies approved to offer a service direct to the public. Accreditation is provided by the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission. See our National Police Certificate accredited bodies page for links to lodge screening requests. 

Immunisation Risk for this position is - Category B (indirect contact with blood or body substances)

Lead, support, and develop a team of AML analysts.
Manage workloads, queues, and service level commitments.
Conduct quality assurance reviews and provide coaching and feedback.
Review and assess complex AML alerts, customer due diligence, and screening outcomes.

Produce management reporting and performance metrics.

5+ years' experience in AML, financial crime, or compliance operations.
